verdicts.reason: A: the headline wraps and leaves 'Yet' on its own line; the legal text floats on the left as a competing block; the eyebrow 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' is pushed below the body copy; the white SOLSTICE wordmark disappears on the cream background; the dark band is a leftover stub in the top right. B fixes the headline wrap, but it keeps the same invisible logo, stub band, orphaned divider line and eyebrow placed after the body, and its small CTA is jammed against the fine print in the bottom-left corner.

A: the headline sits on one line, but the CTA is small and crammed bottom-left beside the legal text, the logo wordmark is invisible, and the eyebrow sits below the body. Still, B's CTA is clearly prominent and grouped with the legal text in a right column, which reads as more intentional.

A has the shared flaws: an invisible white wordmark, a stub dark band, a stray divider, the eyebrow below the body, and a small CTA crowded by the legal text. B is worse for the brand and the hierarchy: the logo has shrunk to a tiny speck in the bottom right next to a tiny CTA, and the fine print floats as an unanchored paragraph in the upper right with large dead areas around it, even though the left text block is clean.
